log.msg: REPRODUCED, no AI2 even needed: fresh /framework/, click the rail's AI link once — the page shows only the h1 'AI', .v3 count 0. Screenshot matched the owner's report pixel for pixel (title changed, body empty). AI -> AI2 -> AI just hits the same bug on its first leg; AI2 -> AI direct and AI -> AI2 -> back all hit it too, since it is about the FIRST soft click onto AI in a session, not about AI2 at all.

CAUSE, found not guessed. ai/page.js's content() calls v/3/page.js's draw_board(this), which only draws when `location.pathname === page.url`. Router.go() (core/Router/Router.js) runs `this.activate(page)` — which runs content() synchronously — and only calls `history.pushState()` AFTER that returns (comment: 'Load first, push second, so a failed navigation leaves no history entry'). So on the very first soft click onto a page gated this way, location.pathname is still the PREVIOUS page's, the guard always loses, draw_board() never runs, and because Page.render() caches this.view, content() never runs again — the page is blank for the rest of the session. The board-declutter comment already in ai/page.js claimed this race 'reads correctly both ways' (2026-09-22 17:49); it does not, on the losing side. A full page load / deep link never hits this, because location is already correct before any JS runs — which is why the mastermind's earlier direct shot of /framework/ai/ at 18:19 looked fine.

FIX, one place, ai/page.js content() only — did not touch v/3/page.js (board-declutter owns it right now) or the Router (didn't need to). draw_board(this) still runs synchronously first (covers a cold load, where location is already right, with no extra frame of delay). If that lost the race (this.board_drawn still false), retry once via requestAnimationFrame — by then go() has returned and pushState has landed, so draw_board()'s own UNCHANGED location check reads correctly. This mirrors the fix already used for the symmetric bug going the other way (v/3/page.js's deactivated() -> requestAnimationFrame -> draw_board(root), from board-declutter today). A page that really is a hidden ancestor of a deeper deep link still reads wrong on both tries and correctly never draws.

PROOF, all headless against a private worktree server (port 8096; ai/usage.json copied in locally only, gitignored, not part of the patch — the worktree doesn't carry gitignored runtime files and its absence 404'd until copied). Sequence A (fresh /framework/, AI -> AI2 -> AI): v3=1 after the first AI click, AI2 shows 'Hello world', v3=1 again back on AI. Sequence B (fresh /framework/, AI2 -> AI direct): v3=1. Sequence C (fresh /framework/, AI -> AI2 -> browser Back): v3=1 visible and correct on screen (screenshot: the days board, right where it should be) after Back. Deep link /framework/ai/ (cold, full load): v3=1, exactly once, matching board-declutter's own fix. Zero console errors on any step across 27 steps. Screenshots in shots/.

FINDING, logged not fixed (outside my fence — ai/v/3/page.js belongs to board-declutter's task today, and this is a different, non-blanking symptom from the one I was asked to fix). Sequence C's DOM has TWO .v3 nodes after the Back button (only one is visible; the other is the ai singleton's own hidden board, still in the tree because 'going up the chain activates nothing' means Router never deactivates it, and the fresh /framework/ai/days/ child page mounts as a sibling, not a replacement). Same class the board-declutter comment in ai/page.js already accepts for the deep-link case ('the only cost was ever the hidden work, never wrong content on screen') — just reachable a second way, via Back after a soft click had already drawn the root's own board. Nothing wrong on screen (screenshot c1-back-button-to-ai.png), no console error, but it is a real duplicate board (duplicate fetches/EventSource) worth folding into whoever next touches v/3/page.js's view-url routing.

LANDING deviation, logged as the skill's own guidance says to: the launcher's exact command, `git diff --binary carry-in`, resolved `carry-in` to a stale TAG pointing at an old ancestor commit (not this worktree's own HEAD, which happens to share the same commit-message word) and produced a 6269-line diff touching dozens of unrelated files. Recovered by reading the main tree's current file directly, confirming it textually matched my worktree's OWN starting point (it did), and re-applying the identical two edits by hand against the main tree path with the Edit tool instead of the patch pipeline. Same two files, same content, verified by grepping for my own comment markers and by node --check.

LANDED AND PROVEN on the real main tree, port 8123, reload hold taken for the writes and released after. All three owner-reported sequences pass: AI -> AI2 -> AI shows the days board every time (not blank); AI2 -> AI direct shows it; AI -> AI2 -> browser Back shows it (screenshot: the full board, correctly selected in the rail). The bare /framework/ai/ deep link still mounts .v3 exactly once. Zero console errors across all 27 steps of the proof run. AI 2's own content has moved on since this task started (inbox-model landed a real board there, no longer 'Hello world') - unrelated to this fix, confirmed it still renders correctly either way.

assign.outcome:
**Clicking the rail's AI link went blank because of a one-frame race with the browser's own url, and it is fixed.** The sequence: any FIRST soft click onto `/framework/ai/` in a session (AI -> AI2 -> AI hits it on the very first leg, and so does AI2 -> AI direct, and AI -> AI2 -> Back) left only the title "AI" showing, nothing below it — reproduced headless, pixel-for-pixel the owner's own screenshot. The cause: `ai/page.js`'s board-drawing guard compares `location.pathname` to its own url, but `Router.go()` runs that check synchronously, before it calls `history.pushState()` — so on that first click the browser's address bar hasn't caught up yet, the guard always loses, and because the page's view is cached, it never gets a second chance and stays blank for the rest of the session. The fix, in `ai/page.js` alone: try to draw immediately (covers a normal page reload, where the url is already right), and if that lost the race, try again one animation frame later, by which point the url has caught up and the same unchanged check passes — the same trick the code already used for the symmetric bug going the other way. Proven on the real site (port 8123): all three sequences now show the board every time, the direct `/framework/ai/` link still mounts its board exactly once, and 27 headless steps produced zero console errors.

One related finding, not fixed here because it lives in a file another task owns today: going back with the browser's Back button after visiting AI leaves a second, hidden copy of the board in the page (nothing wrong on screen, no error, just wasted work) — logged in the task log for whoever next touches `ai/v/3/page.js`'s view-url routing.
